statement: Five years ago, Tom was 3 times as old as his sister. In five years' time, he will be twice as old as she will be then. How old is Tom now?

choices.misconception: I added 5 years to Tom's age in the future clue but forgot to add them to his sister's age.
I solved correctly but gave Tom's age five years ago.
I solved correctly but gave Tom's age in five years' time.
I solved correctly but gave his sister's age instead of Tom's.

hints: Both people's ages change by the same number of years.
Translate into equations: call the ages now t and s, write each clue using t - 5 and s - 5 for the past and t + 5 and s + 5 for the future, then solve together.
t - 5 = 3(s - 5) and t + 5 = 2(s + 5). Write t from each and set them equal.

solutions.reliable: Let Tom be t and his sister s now. Five years ago: t - 5 = 3(s - 5), so t = 3s - 10. In five years: t + 5 = 2(s + 5), so t = 2s + 5. Then 3s - 10 = 2s + 5, so s = 15 and t = 35. Check: five years ago they were 30 and 10, and 30 is 3 times 10; in five years they will be 40 and 20, and 40 is twice 20. The transferable idea: shift every person's age by the same number of years, then reread the question to see whose age, and when.
solutions.elegant: Back-solve from the choices: if Tom is 35, five years ago he was 30, so his sister was 10 and is now 15. In five years they will be 40 and 20, which works.

whyOnTest: Age problems test setting up equations at different times, and most wrong choices answer for the wrong person or the wrong year.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
